3468-poems-by-the-way.creator: Unknown
3468-poems-by-the-way.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Pass the wind-flowers and the bays, Through the garth, and go our ways, Wandering down among the meads Till our very joyance needs Rest at last; till we shall come To that Sun-god's lonely home, Lonely on the hill-side grey, Whence the sheep have gone away; Lonely till the feast-time is, When with prayer and praise of bliss, Thither comes the country side.

arxiv-2209-13908.title: Lyapunov stability analysis of rigid body systems with multiple contacts by sums-of-squares programming
arxiv-2209-13908.creator: Péter L. Várkonyi
arxiv-2209-13908.description: Abstract Reliable quasi-static object manuipulation and robotic locomotion require verification of the stability of equilibria under rigid contacts and friction. In a recent paper, M. Posa, M. Tobenkin, and R. Tedrake demonstrated that sums-of-squares (SOS) programming can be used to verify Lyapunov stability via Lyapunov’s direct method.

arxiv-2306-01084.title: Exploration on HuBERT with Multiple Resolutions
arxiv-2306-01084.creator: Jiatong Shi 1 , Yun Tang 2 , Hirofumi Inaguma 2 , Hongyu Gong 2 , Juan Pino 2 , Shinji Watanabe 1
arxiv-2306-01084.description: Abstract Hidden-unit BERT (HuBERT) is a widely-used self-supervised learning (SSL) model in speech processing. However, we argue that its fixed 20ms resolution for hidden representations would not be optimal for various speech-processing tasks since their attributes (e.g., speaker characteristics and semantics) are based on different time scales.

arxiv-2403-19847.title: Strategic Complemantarities as stochastic control under sticky price
arxiv-2403-19847.creator: Lambert Dong
arxiv-2403-19847.description: Abstract We examine how monetary shocks spread throughout an economic model characterized by sticky prices and general equilibrium, where the pricing strategies of firms are interlinked, fostering a mutually beneficial relationship. In this dynamic equilibrium, pricing choices of firms are influenced by overall economic factors, which are themselves affected by these decisions.

arxiv-2405-01808.title: GRAND Massive Parallel Decoding Framework for Low Latency in Beyond 5G
arxiv-2405-01808.creator: Danilo Gligoroski, Sahana Sridhar, Katina Kralevska
arxiv-2405-01808.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Danilo Gligoroski, Sahana Sridhar, Katina Kralevska. We propose a massive parallel decoding GRAND framework. The framework introduces two novelties: 1. A likelihood function for M M -QAM demodulated signals that effectively reduces the symbol error pattern space from 𝒪 ⁡ ( 5 N / log 2 ⁡ M ) \mathcal{O}(5^{N/\log_{2}M}) down to 𝒪 ⁡ ( 4 N / log 2 ⁡ M ) \mathcal{O}(4^{N/\log_{2}M}) ; and 2.

arxiv-2408-05351.title: Distributed Quantum Computing for Chemical Applications Thanks: We would like to acknowledge the Government of Canada’s New Frontiers in Research Fund (NFRF), for grant NFRFE-2022-00226, and the Quantum Software Consortium (QSC), financed under grant #ALLRP587590-23 from the National Sciences and En
arxiv-2408-05351.creator: Grier M. Jones 1 2 3 ,Hans-Arno Jacobsen 2
arxiv-2408-05351.description: Abstract In recent years, interest in quantum computing has increased due to technological advances in quantum hardware and algorithms. Despite the promises of quantum advantage, the applicability of quantum devices has been limited to few qubits on hardware that experiences decoherence due to noise. One proposed method to get around this challenge is distributed quantum computing (DQC).

arxiv-2409-19188.title: Machine learning surrogate models for particle insertions and element substitutions
arxiv-2409-19188.creator: Ryosuke Jinnouchi
arxiv-2409-19188.description: Abstract Two machine learning-aided thermodynamic integration schemes to compute the chemical potentials of atoms and molecules have been developed and compared. One is the particle insertion method, and the other combines particle insertion with element substitution. In the former method, the species is gradually inserted into the liquid, and its chemical potential is computed.

arxiv-2505-03788.title: Calibrating Uncertainty Quantification of Multi-Modal LLMs using Grounding
arxiv-2505-03788.creator: Trilok Padhi* Ramneet Kaur*, Adam D. Cobb, Manoj Acharya, Anirban Roy, Colin Samplawski, Brian Matejek, Alexander M. Berenbeim, Nathaniel D. Bastian, Susmit Jha
arxiv-2505-03788.description: Abstract We introduce a novel approach for calibrating uncertainty quantification (UQ) tailored for multi-modal large language models (LLMs). Existing state-of-the-art UQ methods rely on consistency among multiple responses generated by the LLM on an input query under diverse settings. However, these approaches often report higher confidence in scenarios where the LLM is consistently incorrect.

arxiv-2505-19435.title: Route to Reason: Adaptive Routing for LLM and Reasoning Strategy Selection
arxiv-2505-19435.creator: Zhihong Pan, Kai Zhang, Yuze Zhao, Yupeng Han
arxiv-2505-19435.description: Abstract The inherent capabilities of a language model (LM) and the reasoning strategies it employs jointly determine its performance in reasoning tasks. While test-time scaling is regarded as an effective approach to tackling complex reasoning tasks, it incurs substantial computational costs and often leads to "overthinking", where models become trapped in "thought pitfalls".

arxiv-2508-17234.title: ClaimGen-CN: A Large-scale Chinese Dataset for Legal Claim Generation
arxiv-2508-17234.creator: Siying Zhou, Yiquan Wu, Hui Chen, Xavier Hu, Kun Kuang, Adam Jatowt, Ming Hu, Chunyan Zheng, Fei Wu
arxiv-2508-17234.description: Abstract Legal claims refer to the plaintiff’s demands in a case and are essential to guiding judicial reasoning and case resolution. While many works have focused on improving the efficiency of legal professionals, the research on helping non-professionals (e.g., plaintiffs) remains unexplored. This paper explores the problem of legal claim generation based on the given case’s facts.

pmc-10701754.creator: Ako Matsuhashi, Kei Yanai, Satoshi Koizumi, Gakushi Yoshikawa
pmc-10701754.description: BACKGROUNDIntracranial arteriovenous fistula (AVF) is a rare disease, defined as anastomoses between cerebral or meningeal arteries and dural venous sinuses or cortical veins. With the development of new agents and devices, endovascular embolization has been considered safe and effective in a majority of cases. However, cases that require direct surgery do exist.

pmc-10709956.title: A high quality Aotearoa New Zealand dietary pattern adapting a Mediterranean diet for metabolic health: a feasibility study
pmc-10709956.creator: Amber Parry-Strong, Richard Gearry, Troy L. Merry, Mark Weatherall, Cheryl Davies, Anna Worthington, Rhiane Bishop, Summer Rangimaarie Wright, Fiona E. Lithander, Meika Foster, Jeremy Krebs
pmc-10709956.description: AimTo assess the feasibility of a family-based dietary intervention study using a meal kit home delivery service, in people at risk of cardio-metabolic disease.MethodsA 12-week dietary intervention feasibility study of adults (termed the index participants) at increased risk of metabolic and cardiovascular disease, enriched for Māori who are indigenous New Zealanders.

pmc-11656257.title: Origin, Distribution, and Influential Factors of Organic Acids in Deep and Ultradeep Clastic Reservoirs within the Fukang Sag of the Junggar Basin
pmc-11656257.creator: Wenjun Pang, Jing Li, Shixin Zhou, Liangliang Liu, Yaoyu Li, Hao Wang, Gengrong Chen
pmc-11656257.description: In deep and ultradeep clastic reservoirs, secondary porosity functions as the primary space for hydrocarbon storage, intricately associated with the dissolution processes of water-soluble organic acids (WSOAs). However, conventional theories concerning secondary porosity predominantly emphasize medium-depth or shallow reservoirs, lacking a thorough investigation into how WSOA-driven mechanisms affect deeper strata formations.

pmc-11678907.title: Clearance of Intracellular Pathogens with Hyaluronic Acid Nanomicelles Responsive to H2S and pH
pmc-11678907.creator: Jun Luo, Hui Huang, Junfeng Jiang, Wenyu Zheng, Peng Chen, Hongjin Bai, Xin Wang, Xiaolong Ji
pmc-11678907.description: Hyaluronic acid (HA) is an acidic mucopolysaccharide of animal origin composed of repeating disaccharide units of N-acetylglucosamine and glucuronic acid. Due to its excellent biocompatibility, biodegradability, and selective affinity for CD44 receptors on cell surfaces, HA is widely employed as a drug carrier.

pmc-11715088.title: Impact of Physical Frailty on Cognitive, Psychological, Social, Functional Outcomes, Multimorbidity and Brain Structure among Aging Rural Indians
pmc-11715088.creator: Jonas S Sundarakumar, Pravin Sahadevan, Raghav Prasad, Pooja Rai, Hitesh Pradhan, Sakshi Arora, Sumedha Mitra, Priya Chatterjee, Aishwarya B Hiremath, Palash K Malo, Ramya Burra, CBR‐SANSCOG Study Team
pmc-11715088.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundThough frailty is common in aging, its impact on varied health outcomes has been grossly understudied among rural Indians. We aimed to cross‐sectionally examine the impact of physical frailty on 13 health outcomes and brain structure in this population.MethodParticipants (n=5302) were non‐demented, aging individuals (≥45 years) from the ongoing Srinivaspura Aging Neuro Senescence and Cognition (SANSCOG) cohort in rural southern India. Physical frailty was evaluated using a modified version of Fried's criteria, and participants were classified as non‐frail, pre‐frail and frail.

pmc-11793158.title: The effects of marine heatwaves on a coral reef snapper: insights into aerobic and anaerobic physiology and recovery
pmc-11793158.creator: Shannon J McMahon, Philip L Munday, Jennifer M Donelson, Katharina Ruthsatz
pmc-11793158.description: Marine heatwaves (MHW) are intensifying, posing a grave threat to coral reefs. We exposed Lutjanus carponotatus to MHW conditions (+1°C and + 2°C) for 4 weeks and found increased oxygen consumption and recovery time, among other physiological changes. Interestingly, several effects persisted for at least 2 weeks post-MHW.

pmc-12466941.title: Exploratory Insights into Gastric Cancer Metabolism Through Amino Acid and Acylcarnitine Profiling in Plasma Samples
pmc-12466941.creator: Ștefan Ursu, Cristina-Paula Ursu, Luisa-Gabriela Bogos, Ioana-Ecaterina Pralea, Radu-Cristian Moldovan, Florin Zaharie, Zeno Spârchez, Răzvan Alexandru Ciocan, Rodica Sorina Pop, Cătălin Ioan Bodea, Claudia Diana Gherman, Cristina-Adela Iuga, Nadim Al Hajjar, Chi Chun Wong
pmc-12466941.description: Background: Gastric cancer ranks fifth among the most prevalent malignancies, with poor prognosis due to limited early-stage diagnosis. Metabolic reprogramming plays a central role in GC development, sustaining carcinogenic processes. Methods: In this study, flow-injection tandem mass spectrometry was used to analyse plasma amino acids and acylcarnitines in 62 gastric cancer patients and 70 healthy individuals.

pmc-12522803.title: FocaL mass drug administration for Plasmodium vivax malaria elimination (FLAME): study protocol for an open-label cluster randomized controlled trial in Peru
pmc-12522803.creator: Sydney R Fine, Veronica Soto Calle, Astrid Altamirano Quiroz, Hugo Rodriquez Ferruci, Paulo Manrique, Xue Wu, Gabriel Carrasco Escobar, Jade Benjamin-Chung, Adam Bennett, Sarah Auburn, Ric N Price, Bryan Greenhouse, J Kevin Baird, Gonzalo J Domingo, Michelle E Roh, Angel Rosas, Alejandro Llanos-Cuen
pmc-12522803.description: BackgroundOutside of sub-Saharan Africa, Plasmodium vivax has become the dominant species of malaria. Focal mass drug administration (fMDA) is a potential strategy to support elimination efforts, but controlled studies are lacking.MethodsThe FocaL mass drug Administration for Plasmodium vivax Malaria Elimination (FLAME) study is a 3-year cluster randomized controlled trial to determine the impact and safety of fMDA to reduce P.

pmc-12620480.title: Interaction of repetition and retention interval influences the transfer effect after answer feedback for episodic memory
pmc-12620480.creator: Lingwei Wang, Jiongjiong Yang
pmc-12620480.description: IntroductionRetrieval practice with answer feedback is an efficient way to enhance episodic memory, but previous studies fail to find a robust transfer of learning for non-trained information. The aim of this study was to clarify the boundary conditions for the transfer effect after answer feedback.

pmc-12703848.title: Menthol cigarette alternative products: Awareness, use, and substitution intentions among adults who smoke menthol cigarettes
pmc-12703848.creator: Christina N. Kyriakos, Grace Kong, Akshika Sharma, Meghan E. Morean, Sakinah C. Suttiratana, Krysten W. Bold
pmc-12703848.description: Background:Menthol cigarette alternative products (e.g., menthol accessories, non-menthol cooling cigarettes) have entered the market and may bypass menthol cigarette restrictions. Understanding awareness, use, and substitution intentions if menthol cigarette sales are prohibited is important for assessing their potential to undermine the public health benefit of such policies.

pmc-13145816.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A604 ELECTRICAL STIMULATION IMPROVES STRENGTH AND ACTIVITY AFTER STROKE: FINDINGS FROM A COCHRANE SYSTEMATIC REVIEW
pmc-13145816.creator: Katharine Scrivener, Louise Ada, Joanne Glinsky, Simone Dorsch, Serena Jamieson, Sarah Brighton-Hall, Laura McCredie, Ashleigh Hanekom, Natasha Lannin
pmc-13145816.description: Background and aimsElectrical stimulation is commonly used for motor rehabilitation after stroke, but its benefits and harms were uncertain. The aim of our systematic review was to evaluate whether electrical stimulation improves strength and activity, compared with sham, no intervention, or alternative approaches. We also examined effects on participation, quality of life, and adverse events.

pmc-13151109.title: Bacillus velezensis mitigates chronic LPS-induced lung injury of broilers via microbiota-driven isoflavone production and NF-κB/PPAR-γ axis modulation
pmc-13151109.creator: Xunbozan Zhang, Xuan Liu, Ye Xu, Dadan Liu, Ying Chen, Christopher Peterson Daniel, Ruixiao Mao, Liang Chen
pmc-13151109.description: BackgroundChronic exposure to low‑dose lipopolysaccharide (LPS) in poultry farming environments induces persistent respiratory inflammation, resulting in lung injury and impaired growth performance in broilers. Bacillus velezensis (BV) is a probiotic with known antibacterial and immunomodulatory activities, yet its role in respiratory health remains poorly understood.

pmc-13274620.title: NPAS3-regulated astrocyte mitochondrial bioenergetics is required for cognition

pmc-13336258.title: Bridging environmental pollution and immune dysregulation: How microplastics disrupt gut homeostasis to promote allergic diseases
pmc-13336258.creator: Xu Zhang, Ke Liu, Zhiqiang Zhang, Xinyu Huang, Mengyuan Liu, Daoming Bai, Rui Yang, Chunping Yang
pmc-13336258.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Parallel increases in microplastic (MP) pollution and allergic diseases suggest an environmental link in allergy pathogenesis. While intestinal barrier dysfunction and dysbiosis are hallmark features of allergic diseases, the mechanisms by which persistent MPs drive these processes remain unclear. This review proposes a mechanistic pathway where orally ingested MPs disrupt the intestinal barrier through physical and chemical toxicity, precipitating functional dysbiosis. Specifically, MPs suppress key short-chain fatty acid (SCFA)-producing commensals.

pmc-13585584.title: Interim efficacy and preliminary survival outcomes of polatuzumab vedotin in combination for diffuse large B-cell lymphoma: a retrospective real-world study
pmc-13585584.creator: Songshen Liu, Xia Zhao, Xue Shi, Hong Xu, Wei Wang, Lingjie Sun
pmc-13585584.description: PurposeThe standard first-line R-CHOP regimen achieves cure in only approximately 50% of patients. Polatuzumab vedotin (Pola) is a novel antibody-drug conjugate targeting the B-cell receptor component CD79b; however, evidence regarding its real-world efficacy remains relatively limited. This retrospective study aims to evaluate the clinical efficacy of Pola in combination therapy.

uslaw-usc-t10-s7317.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t10-s7317.description: United States Code, Title 10 (Armed Forces); Part II (Personnel); Chapter 741 (Retirement For Length Of Service). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel.
